title: Network pharmacology-based identification of cardamomin as a ferroptosis inhibitor in ischemic stroke via SP1/ALOX5 axis.
authors: Shao, Libo; Gao, Xiaolin; Yu, Wenming; Zhang, Wenwen; Lu, Xing
one_liner_zh: 该文通过网络药理学和分子对接研究豆蔻明经SP1/ALOX5轴抑制缺血性脑卒中铁死亡，虽涉及TF-DNA结合（SP1-ALOX5启动子）和分子对接，但核心是药物机制与疾病表型，非TF-DNA互作建模方法研究，与本课题关联有限。
abstract: BACKGROUND: Ischemic stroke (IS) causes high mortality and disability, yet current thrombolytic therapy is constrained by narrow time windows and side effects. Ferroptosis has recently as a critical pathological mechanism in cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury, but effective modulators remain lacking. Cardamomin shows neuroprotective potential; however, its role in regulating ferroptosis during IS is unknown and warrants urgent investigation. METHODS: Potential targets of cardamomin were identified using bioinformatics tools. KEGG enrichment analysis and molecular docking were performed. Cell viability and apoptosis were assessed by MTT and flow cytometry. Inflammatory cytokines and ferroptosis markers were detected by specific commercial kits. Western blot, dual-luciferase reporter assay, and chromatin immunoprecipitation were employed to investigate the SP1-ALOX5 regulatory axis. For in vivo validation, a middle cerebral artery occlusion model was established. Evaluations included neurological deficits, infarct volume by TTC staining, histopathology by HE staining, and molecular expression analysis. RESULTS: ALOX5 was identified as a key ferroptosis-related target. Cardamomin alleviated OGD/R-induced injury by restoring cell viability, suppressing apoptosis and inflammation, and reversing ferroptotic changes. Molecular docking confirmed a strong binding affinity between cardamomin and ALOX5 (-7.6 kcal/mol). Mechanistically, transcription factor SP1 transcriptionally activated ALOX5 by binding to its promoter, and cardamomin downregulated the SP1/ALOX5 axis and subsequently activated the PI3K/AKT pathway. In vivo, cardamomin reduced cerebral infarction, improved neurological function, and inhibited inflammation and ferroptosis. CONCLUSION: Cardamomin attenuates neuronal ferroptosis and ischemic injury by inhibiting the SP1/ALOX5 axis and activating the PI3K/AKT pathway, providing a novel therapeutic candidate for IS.
abstract_zh: 背景：缺血性卒中（Ischemic stroke, IS）导致高死亡率和致残率，而当前溶栓治疗受限于狭窄的时间窗和副作用。铁死亡（ferroptosis）最近被认为是脑缺血再灌注损伤中的关键病理机制，但有效的调节剂仍缺乏。豆蔻明（Cardamomin）显示出神经保护潜力；然而，其在IS中调节铁死亡的作用尚不清楚，亟需研究。方法：利用生物信息学工具鉴定豆蔻明的潜在靶点。进行了KEGG富集分析和分子对接（molecular docking）。通过MTT和流式细胞术评估细胞活力和凋亡。使用特定商业试剂盒检测炎症细胞因子和铁死亡标志物。采用Western blot、双荧光素酶报告基因实验和染色质免疫沉淀（chromatin immunoprecipitation）研究SP1-ALOX5调控轴。体内验证中，建立了大脑中动脉闭塞模型。评估包括神经功能缺损、TTC染色梗死体积、HE染色组织病理学及分子表达分析。结果：ALOX5被鉴定为关键的铁死亡相关靶点。豆蔻明通过恢复细胞活力、抑制凋亡和炎症、逆转铁死亡变化，减轻了OGD/R诱导的损伤。分子对接确认豆蔻明与ALOX5之间具有强结合亲和力（-7.6 kcal/mol）。机制上，转录因子SP1通过结合其启动子转录激活ALOX5，而豆蔻明下调SP1/ALOX5轴，随后激活PI3K/AKT通路。体内实验中，豆蔻明减少脑梗死、改善神经功能，并抑制炎症和铁死亡。结论：豆蔻明通过抑制SP1/ALOX5轴并激活PI3K/AKT通路，减轻神经元铁死亡和缺血性损伤，为IS提供了新的治疗候选药物。
